claims.statement: packages/openwiki/openwiki-core is an in-fork port of the openwiki 0.4.3 deterministic engine core (MIT-licensed, attribution preserved in the module headers): the fork removed the DeepAgents/CLI coupling so the engine runs in-process behind a minimal WikiFs filesystem seam with no external openwiki CLI, and repositories written by either engine are interoperable because the on-disk formats are identical.

The engine core is a pure TypeScript library (only zod + yaml deps) organized as src/*: Lifecycle (begin/submit_plan/next_page/submit_page/finish with a durable .run.json checkpoint, git source fingerprinting, update no-op detection, and a .page-manifest.json ledger), Claims (add/confirm/update/retract mutations, .claims/ sidecar persistence, and a repository evidence resolver mapping repo://path#L20-L48 resources to repo-lines-v1:sha256: versions), OKF (v0.2 front matter validation/repair, generated-event origin, index sync), Validation (Mermaid fences with graceful heuristic fallback, wiki-internal-link validation with broken-link stamping), Setup + fs (.openwikiignore, INSTRUCTIONS.md goal, WikiFs/createNodeWikiFs seam), and Integration (HostSessionManager + zod protocol).

tool-openwiki is one Cordis agent-plane plugin mounting as a preset or profile-patch row that injects tools + systemPrompt and registers no service of its own, exposing the five lifecycle tools openwiki_begin, openwiki_submit_plan, openwiki_next_page, openwiki_submit_page, and openwiki_finish.

openwiki_begin starts or resumes a durable run (.run.json) over a Git repository root and returns status=noop for clean updates; openwiki_submit_plan validates and durably persists the ordered PageJob queue (init requires /openwiki/quickstart.md, paths normalized); openwiki_next_page returns the first pending job; openwiki_submit_page proves the complete Claim set against the written page (front matter repair, Claims resolution, durable verification); openwiki_finish performs deterministic finalization including deletions, Mermaid validation, index sync, link validation, generated-event origin, Claims finalization, and .run.json removal.
The tool configuration is id/name plus config host (stable host identity recorded in run metadata) and producerActor (origin actor for engine-owned finalizers).

The five lifecycle schemas encode the exact resumable protocol (explicit root+mode begin, a final non-replaceable ordered plan, per-job claims with id reuse/retraction conventions, and a finish that requires every job complete), and results are small JSON views (changedPaths, claimIssues, completions, no-op status).

The prompt section is one openwiki:tools card: the required lifecycle sequence, durable/resumable run semantics, the rule that every material Claim carries a repository evidence resource, exact claim reconciliation (preserve id/statement/evidence of unchanged claims, reuse id for revision, omit to retract), and the hook to use codebase-memory for structural discovery instead of file-by-file repository scans.

Engine limitations: git is required (source fingerprinting, update windows, and root resolution shell out to git), Mermaid/jsdom peers are optional (without them validation degrades to heuristic fence checks), upstream's CI workflow and source connectors are intentionally not ported, and there is no home-directory onboarding store (the wiki goal is read from the repository's own openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md).
